items.title: Popular pizza place closed due to health violations in Mississauga
items.summary: A popular restaurant in Mississauga is temporarily closed for failing a health inspection. Karachi Pizza, located at 812 Britannia Rd W, was inspected and shut down on Tuesday, Sept. 22. The fusion cuisine restaurant specializes in Karachi style gourmet pan pizzas. According to the inspection report, the restaurant did not properly store food to prevent contamination or adulteration and did not take adequate measures to prevent pests, leading to health risks. The report also alleges that the restaurant did not provide sufficient lighting or maintain non-food contact surfaces in clean, sanitary condition. The restaurant is closed and may reopen later after passing a follow-up inspection. Peel Public Health regularly inspects restaurants in the region, issuing a green card if the inspection is passed, a yellow card for a conditional pass (minor infractions), and a red card if significant health risks are found. A restaurant that’s issued a red card is forced to close until it can pass a follow-up inspection.

items.title: This pub was once a popular movie theatre in Mississauga
items.summary: A former movie theatre in Mississauga received approval for a heritage designation in Mississauga. The building at 75 Lakeshore Rd. E. in Port Credit is now home to The Crooked Cue pub and pool hall, but it was once a popular movie theatre. Farrow and Sons built the Vogue Theatre on a vacant lot at 75 Lakeshore Rd. E. in 1937, according to a report to the City of Mississauga Heritage Advisory Committee. The theatre seated 500 people during a popular time for movie-going. The Port Credit Businessmen’s Association had lobbied for a movie house in the village to compete with New Toronto (Etobicoke) nightlife. Oakville also had a movie theatre by this time, according to the report. Before this theatre was built, people attended Clarke Hall, which screened silent films, but the talkies of the late 1920s did not do as well at this venue. It took two months to build the new theatre. The brick building included a cream and white street front and marquee with Art Deco ornamentation at the top of the façade. The upper level was rented to a salon and dentist.

items.title: Bigger fines drive down summer parking ticket numbers on Mississauga’s waterfront
items.summary: The number of parking tickets issued in Mississauga’s waterfront neighbourhoods during late spring and summer has decreased by hundreds since seasonal fines were hiked to $100 in 2021, the city says. The City of Mississauga has for the past five years more than doubled fines for illegally parking and stopping in areas south of Lakeshore Road — dubbed the Lakefront Increased Penalty Zone — between May 1 and the end of September. The annual initiative is intended to discourage illegal parking in hopes of reducing traffic congestion during the year’s busiest months on and near Mississauga’s waterfront. com. City officials have also said the waterfront areas become busy during the spring and summer months “and draw thousands of residents and visitors. com show. As of Sept. 16, 3,241 penalty notices had been handed out so far during the 2026 Lakefront Increased Penalty Zone initiative, which concludes next Wednesday.

items.title: Dozens of Overnight Vehicle Break-Ins Across Mississauga End With One Arrest and a Continued Search
items.summary: According to Peel Regional Police, a string of vehicle break-ins that hit neighbourhoods across Mississauga between September 3 and September 6 has led to one arrest, with officers still searching for a second suspect. Police say the overnight break-ins involved 71 vehicles that were entered unlawfully, though no vehicles were taken and none were occupied at the time. Investigators allege valuables were stolen from inside the vehicles during the spree. A 34-year-old man with no fixed address has been charged with 46 counts of attempting to commit an indictable offence, 16 counts of theft under $5,000, 15 counts of mischief over $5,000 and one count of theft over $5,000, police say. He was also taken into custody on two outstanding warrants tied to separate fraud investigations, according to police. Peel police say they are still looking for a 34-year-old woman believed to have been involved alongside him in the break-ins.

The review will examine potential tax relief measures, economic development initiatives and investment programs aimed at supporting local businesses and protecting jobs. The motion builds on the City’s existing trade response efforts, including support for export diversification, local supply chains and funding applications designed to help Mississauga businesses access new markets beyond the United States. Council directed staff to review how Mississauga regulates businesses involved in the sale and distribution of tobacco, vapour and related nicotine products. The review will explore opportunities to strengthen municipal licensing requirements, improve compliance monitoring and support efforts to prevent youth access to these products. Staff will work with Peel Public Health and other stakeholders to examine licensing, inspections, enforcement and education measures before reporting back to Council with recommendations. Council approved a reduction in the park enhancement contribution associated with a planned townhouse development at 2020 and 2040 Camilla Road. The adjustment is intended to help facilitate housing construction while recognizing that the development will provide more on-site amenity space than originally required. The original approval required a $450,000 contribution toward improvements to Hancock Woodlands Park. Council reduced that amount to $225,000 after considering changes to city-wide amenity area requirements and the developer’s commitment to move forward with construction in a timely manner.

items.title: Policorner Sets October 5 Date for a Mississauga Mayoral Debate Watched Well Beyond City Hall
items.summary: According to Policorner, a publication focused on Ontario provincial politics, the outlet will host a debate among Mississauga's leading mayoral candidates on Monday, October 5, at the Mississauga Civic Centre. Policorner says it decided to hold the 90-minute debate because the race has drawn unusually heavy provincial attention, given that it features two of only three people to have held the mayor's job since 1978. Premier Doug Ford weighed in on the race months before it began, telling reporters at a Mississauga construction site in March that he would send support to back Mayor Carolyn Parrish, according to Policorner. The outlet notes the contest pits Parrish, who has backing from Ford and his caucus, against her predecessor, a three-term mayor who left to lead the provincial Liberals and has spent much of the past three years opposing the Ford government. Two other candidates who finished second and third in the previous election are also competing for many of the same organizers and networks, Policorner reports.

items.title: 525 native trees and shrubs planted in Mississauga at TD Tree Days
items.summary: Volunteers helped put down roots for a greener Mississauga at Courtneypark Athletic Fields. While leaves will soon begin to fall this season, volunteers are helping grow Mississauga’s urban forest one tree at a time. 125 volunteers signed up to plant 525 native trees and shrubs, such as Sugar Maple, White Birch and White Spruce, on September 19 at Courtneypark Athletic Fields as part of TD Tree Days. Not only will the trees add to the city’s greenery, but they will also strengthen local biodiversity. The City selected Courtneypark Athletic Fields as part of a bigger plan to naturalize approximately one hectare of mowed turfgrass. The planting will create new habitat for wildlife, strengthen connections between nearby green spaces and contribute to a healthier, more resilient urban forest. Over time, the trees and shrubs will provide additional benefits such as increased shade, carbon storage and improved air quality. Since 2014, the City’s partnership with TD Tree Days has helped bring volunteers together to restore natural areas and plant thousands of trees and shrubs across Mississauga. These annual events support the City’s broader efforts to expand Mississauga’s urban forest and improve the health of local ecosystems. The planting also supports the City’s One Million Trees program, a key initiative advancing the goals of Mississauga’s Natural Heritage and Urban Forest Strategy by enhancing biodiversity and strengthening the urban forest for future generations. The September 19 event was the first of three TD Tree Days planting events at Courtneypark Athletic Fields.

items.title: Gun call leads to drug-trafficking charges for 3 Mississauga residents, say Peel police
items.summary: The thefts, say police, happened during the early-morning ho… The undercover operation, dubbed Project Red Zone and launch… When officers were called to an armed person complaint on Sept. 7, police say they found a suspect with an illegal gun and a separate magazine containing ammunition. A Mississauga resident, 26, has been charged with four gun crimes as well as four counts of possession for the purpose of trafficking. Three people from Mississauga are facing drug-trafficking charges after officers responded to reports of a man in a vehicle with a gun, say Peel police. When officers were called to an armed person complaint on Sept. 7, police say they found a suspect with an illegal gun and a separate magazine containing ammunition. During that investigation, which happened near Hurontario Street and Dundas Street West in Mississauga, officers also seized a quantity of suspected cocaine and fentanyl with an estimated value of $65,000, say police. A search warrant was then carried out at a Mississauga home, leading to the arrest of three other suspects.

items.title: Families of Victims Set to Address Court as Mississauga Man Faces Sentencing in Assisted-Suicide Case
items.summary: According to INsauga, friends and relatives of people who died after using items purchased online from Kenneth Law are expected to address the court this week as the Mississauga man faces a sentencing hearing. Law pleaded guilty in late May to 14 counts of aiding suicide in the deaths of 14 people across Ontario, including some victims who were minors. That plea came weeks before Law was set to stand trial on those charges along with 14 counts of first-degree murder connected to the same victims, and prosecutors have said they intend to withdraw the murder charges once he is sentenced. A conviction for aiding suicide can carry up to 14 years in prison, and lawyers for the Crown and defence are expected to argue for what each side considers an appropriate sentence. The hearing is also meant to give loved ones of those who died a chance to describe in court how Law's actions affected them. According to an agreed statement of facts read in court, Law ran several websites that sold sodium nitrite and other products that can be used for self-harm, and shipped roughly 1,200 packages to recipients in more than 40 countries, including close to 160 packages sent within Canada.

items.title: Coroner's Jury Rules 2023 Death of Mississauga Senior an Accident, Calls for Crisis-Team Reforms
items.summary: A coroner's inquest jury has ruled the 2023 death of 88-year-old Mississauga resident John Brownlie an accident and issued 18 recommendations aimed at reforming how police and mental health crisis teams respond to similar calls. According to the inquest, Brownlie, a retired schoolteacher, died from complications of a blunt impact neck injury after falling down a flight of stairs during a struggle with a Peel Regional Police officer inside his Mississauga home. The inquest heard that Brownlie had been identified as a candidate for a visit from the Crisis Outreach and Support Team, known as COAST, on September 13, 2023, a day after his wife, Doris, called a crisis line seeking help. Among the jury's recommendations are mandatory body cameras for officers responding to mental health crisis calls and revised protocols for how those officers make first contact. The recommendations are intended to prevent similar deaths during future encounters between police and people in mental health crisis, according to the inquest jury's findings.
